intro: Tennessee learner permits (Class PD) start at age 15. Our Tennessee bank is a verified starter set focused on licensing rules and the hands-free law; road-sign and rules-of-the-road questions are being added.

commonMistakes.text: Thinking you can touch your phone for GPS at a red light. Tennessee requires you to pull over and stop first.
Assuming any adult can supervise a permit driver. The supervising driver must be licensed, at least 21, and sitting beside you.

faq.q: How old do you have to be to get a learner permit in Tennessee?
faq.a: You must be at least 15 and pass the knowledge test and vision screening for a Class D license.

faq.q: How long must I hold my permit before getting a license?
faq.a: If you are under 18, you must hold a valid Class PD for 180 days and meet the Graduated Driver License requirements, including certification of 50 hours of driving.

faq.q: Does Tennessee have an official practice test?
faq.a: Yes. The manual points to official practice knowledge tests at tn.gov/dlpractice.

questions.question: What is the minimum age for a Tennessee Class PD learner permit?
questions.explanation: To obtain a Class PD license, you must have reached the age of 15 and pass the knowledge test and vision screening for a Class D license.
questions.sourceSection: Section A-1: Your License — Class PD Learner Permit

questions.question: A Class PD learner permit holder may drive only when accompanied by:
options: A licensed driver at least 21 years old sitting in the seat beside them
A licensed driver in the back seat
questions.correctAnswer: A licensed driver at least 21 years old sitting in the seat beside them
questions.explanation: A driver with a Class PD license may operate an automobile only when accompanied by a licensed driver who is at least 21 years old and sitting in the seat beside the driver.
questions.sourceSection: Section A-1: Your License — Class PD Learner Permit

questions.question: If you are under 18, how long must you hold a valid Class PD before exchanging it for a license?
questions.explanation: If you are younger than 18, you must have held a valid Class PD for 180 days and meet the Graduated Driver License requirements.
questions.sourceSection: Section A-1: Your License — Class PD Learner Permit

questions.question: Minors applying after the learner-permit period must present certification of how many hours of behind-the-wheel experience?
questions.explanation: The documents checklist requires certification of 50 hours of behind-the-wheel driving experience (form SF-1256) after holding the learner permit for six months.
questions.sourceSection: Section A-2: Applying for Your License — Documents and Forms Checklist

questions.question: What is the minimum age for a Tennessee Class D license?
questions.explanation: To qualify for a Class D license, you must be at least 16 and pass a vision screening, knowledge test, and driving test. Under 18 also requires the Intermediate (GDL) qualifications.
questions.sourceSection: Section A-1: Your License — Class D License

questions.question: Under Tennessee's hands-free law, it is illegal for a driver to:
options: Use a phone with a hands-free system
Hold a cellphone or mobile device with any part of their body
Use a vehicle's built-in GPS set before the trip
questions.correctAnswer: Hold a cellphone or mobile device with any part of their body
questions.explanation: Tennessee's 2019 hands-free law (Public Chapter No. 412) makes it illegal to hold a phone with any part of the body, write, send or read texts, watch or record video, and more.

questions.question: You need to change your phone's GPS route while driving in Tennessee. What should you do?
options: Use the phone at a red light
Pull over to a safe place, come to a full stop, then use the phone
Hold the phone below the dashboard
Ask for help from a passenger in the back seat only
questions.correctAnswer: Pull over to a safe place, come to a full stop, then use the phone
questions.explanation: You are not allowed to touch your phone to use GPS. If you need it, find a safe place to pull over, bring the vehicle to a full stop, and then operate the phone.

questions.question: According to the Tennessee manual, sending or reading a text takes your eyes off the road for a minimum of:
questions.explanation: Sending or reading a text takes your eyes off the road for a minimum of 5 seconds — at 55 mph, like driving the length of a football field with your eyes closed.

questions.question: New residents with a license from another state must get a Tennessee license no later than:
questions.explanation: New or returning residents holding a license from another state must obtain a Tennessee driver license no later than thirty days after establishing residency.
questions.sourceSection: Section A-2: Applying for Your License — New Residents

questions.question: How soon must you notify the Tennessee Department of Safety of an address change?
questions.explanation: State law requires you to notify the Department of Safety within ten days of a residence address change.
questions.sourceSection: Section A-2: Frequently Asked Questions — How Do I Change My Address?

questions.question: A Tennessee hardship (Class H) license may be issued to a minor as young as:
questions.explanation: A Class H hardship license may be issued to a minor who is 14 to operate a Class D vehicle or Class M motorcycle, only in cases of family hardship.
questions.sourceSection: Section A-1: Your License — Class H Hardship

questions.question: A Tennessee Class H hardship license is valid:
options: Only with a parent in the car
Only during daylight hours, for travel to authorized locations
questions.correctAnswer: Only during daylight hours, for travel to authorized locations
questions.explanation: The Class H license is valid only for daylight hours and for travel to authorized locations specified in the approval letter.
questions.sourceSection: Section A-1: Your License — Class H Hardship

questions.question: If you drive without your license in your possession in Tennessee, the fine is:
options: Not less than $2 and no more than $50
questions.correctAnswer: Not less than $2 and no more than $50
questions.explanation: Not having your license with you is a Class D misdemeanor; you may be fined not less than $2.00 and no more than $50.00.
questions.sourceSection: Section A-1: Penalties for Driving Without a License

questions.question: If your Tennessee license has been expired for more than 30 days, the late fee is:
questions.explanation: If your license has expired more than thirty days, there is a $5.00 late fee. After six months the late fee doubles to $10.00.
questions.sourceSection: Section A-2: Frequently Asked Questions — Don't Let Your License Expire
